title: NordBank x Redwood - Security & data residency review
next_steps: Redwood to provide written exception memo for conditional US failover
NordBank to confirm memo acceptable for procurement
Schedule technical deep dive on routing controls
transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2025-02-14
Time: 16:00 CET
Duration: 47 min
Attendees (Redwood): Avery Johnson, Dev Patel, Camila Reyes
Attendees (NordBank): Elin Sjberg, Mikael Lund, Sara Holm

Summary (auto)
- Discussed data residency expectation (EU only) and what happens during failover / incidents.
- Redwood proposed a time bounded exception for US failover with payload logging disabled.

Transcript
[00:00] Avery Johnson: Thanks everyone. Goal today is residency + logging + what regions you need.
[00:41] Mikael Lund: Our baseline is EU only. For us its mostly about where prompts and responses go, and then whats stored.
[01:12] Dev Patel: Under normal operation we pin you to eu-west. The question is failover  we do have regional fallback in the platform.
[02:05] Elin Sjberg: Procurement asked me specifically: can you guarantee it never leaves EU, even during outages?
[02:40] Camila Reyes: If its an absolute never, we have to disable fallback, which can impact uptime. Alternative is an exception: EU primary, conditional US failover only if EU is degraded or during DR testing.
[04:10] Mikael Lund: If we do that exception, what data ends up in the US?
[04:32] Dev Patel: We can disable payload logging for your tenant so prompts/responses are not persisted as logs. You might see request IDs and metrics in the failover region during those windows.
[06:05] Sara Holm: Can you enforce that at tenant level? Not just policy?
[06:18] Dev Patel: Yes, tenant config: region allowlist + gateway logging flags.
[08:02] Elin Sjberg: Okay. Well need it written: duration, who approved, and exactly whats excluded.
[09:20] Avery Johnson: Understood. Well get Security/Legal to sign off a short memo.
...
[45:30] Camila Reyes: Next steps: well send the exception memo, and then well schedule a technical deep dive on the routing controls.
[46:40] Mikael Lund: Great. Thats what we need to unblock.
